text: please fix the app already!! its buggy enough as it is, with reminders routinely just not coming, but since the change for summertime, every planned routine gets delayed an hour, even though it's synchronized and notifications come.. whenever, basically... we pay for this app, it should not work this poorly.
author: Line Haugaard
developer_reply: Hi there, thank you so much for your honest feedback and we’re truly sorry for the frustrating experience you're having🙏Our team is actively investigating this and working on a fix. If you can, please email us at hello@routinery.app so we can prioritize resolving this. Thank you again for your support and patience.

text: The new alarm feature has automatically set VERY aggressive and loud alarms on my phone for the routines. What the heck!? Also it's quite annoying that the icon shows in my top bar of the phone even when I'm not using the app. Otherwise great app, but I have to uninstall it and wait for this to be fixed as the alarms are disturbing me and people around me too much. I'll try to install it again in a month or so to see if it is fixed.
author: Frederik Bramming
developer_reply: Hello Mr. Bramming. First of all, thank you for bringing this inconvenience to our attention, and we apologize for any trouble it has caused. We have identified the issue you reported and are currently working to resolve it. We will do our best to make Routinery more useful as quickly as possible. Thank you for your patience.🙏

text: As others have said, while Routinery has a great concept, that can be invaluable for people with ADHD, the app itself (and especially the Wear OS app) is too broken and unstable to be a reliable tool in the day-to-day. Also, the slightly broken English doesn't help things. An app like RoutineFlow seems to accomplish the same while being infinitely more stable.
